writeup.headline: QIAGEN rates Buy on strong margins and price trend, with a pending EQT takeover shaping the stock.
writeup.thesis: QIAGEN scores 68, a Buy, mainly on quality (82): a gross margin of 62.2%, an operating margin of 22.3%, an FCF margin of 21.7%, stock-based pay at 2.4% of revenue and diluted share count down 2.6% year on year. Trend (76) also helps, with the price 18.2% above its 200-day average and shares 42.0 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days, though shares are down 7.9% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago. The balance sheet scores 73, with net debt at 1.23 times FCF and cash covering 0.66 of debt. Growth is middling at 57: TTM revenue growth of 5.7%, with growth sped up by 5.0 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation was not scored, and news is neutral at 50, dominated by the pending EQT takeover at a €46.50 offer price and a suspended full-year 2026 outlook.
key_risks: The share price is now tied to the EQT deal; if approvals fail or the offer is withdrawn, the stock could fall sharply.
Full-year 2026 guidance is suspended, so there is little company-stated visibility on results.
Preliminary Q3 2026 sales were flat, and growth at TTM revenue growth of 5.7% is modest.
Some brokers, including Barclays and DZ Bank, downgraded after the deal, showing split views on the stock.
what_would_change: A drop of 4 points would move the rating to Hold, for example from weaker trend if the price slips back toward its 200-day average or from negative deal news.
Reaching Strong Buy needs 12 more points, most plausibly from faster revenue growth lifting the growth score from 57.
A completed EQT takeover would remove the stock from public trading, making the rating moot.
Pressure on margins or cash flow would hit the quality score of 82, the main support for the Buy.
